description: We are a team of aspiring innovators passionate about technology, space exploration, and problem-solving. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to create an engaging and interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that introduces young learners to space missions through simulations, challenges, and decision-making. We believe in collaboration, creativity, and continuous learning to turn our ideas into an educational and inspiring experience.
summary:
Outpost Zero is an educational 30-Sol Mars outpost survival and resource-management simulator built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge using React, Vite, and Three.js.

As outpost commander, you explore a first-person 3D Mars base (WASD/Arrows to move, E to interact), drive a rover across Martian terrain under 0.38g low gravity, and manage EVA Suit oxygen outside pressurized tunnels. Across 30 Martian days, you must balance Oxygen, Water, Energy, Food, Spare Parts, and Radiation Protection while handling dynamic Dust Storms, Solar Flares, and Equipment Malfunctions through strategic trade-off decisions.

Every system is grounded in real NASA references—clearly separated from simulated gameplay values—including live/fallback NASA DONKI space-weather alerts, Curiosity MSL-RAD surface radiation benchmarks (~0.64 mSv/day), NASA ECLSS life-support principles, and NASA Mars Fact Sheet atmospheric data (6.36 mb pressure)
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

Outpost Zero is an interactive, educational 30-Sol Mars outpost survival and resource-management simulator. Players step into the role of outpost commander in a first-person 3D Martian habitat (WASD/Arrow keys to move, E to interact) paired with a NASA Mission Control HUD. Walking through pressurized tunnels and airlocks, players inspect stations—Command Console, Life Support/Ventilation, Water Recycler, Greenhouse, Exterior Solar Array, and Radiation Shelter—and drive a Mars rover across the terrain under 0.38g low gravity while managing EVA Suit oxygen outdoors.

Each turn represents one Martian day (Sol). Players manage six interconnected areas—Oxygen, Water, Energy, Food, Spare Parts, and Radiation Protection—while responding to eight dynamic, multi-Sol event types (Dust Storms, Equipment Malfunctions, Greenhouse Problems, Space-Weather Alerts, Solar Flares, Elevated Radiation Conditions, Water Shortages, and Energy Shortages). Every event requires strategic trade-off decisions that affect both the current Sol and future Sols, culminating in a final Mission Success, Partial Success, or Mission Failure evaluation after Sol 30.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Hands-On STEM Learning: Turns abstract planetary science and life-support engineering into tangible cause-and-effect decisions, helping students and space enthusiasts understand why living on Mars is so difficult.

Scientific Honesty: Clearly distinguishes between real/historical NASA data and simulated gameplay values, teaching players the difference between galactic cosmic rays (GCRs), solar energetic particles (SEPs), and solar flares rather than treating radiation as a simple health bar.

Accessible Anywhere: Runs directly in any modern web browser with no downloads or high-end gaming hardware required.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

Languages & Frameworks: JavaScript, React, Vite, Three.js (3D environment & physics), Tailwind CSS, Recharts (telemetry charts)

Data & Persistence: NASA DONKI API (CCMC Docs), Curiosity MSL-RAD historical benchmarks (~0.64 mSv/day), NASA ECLSS subsystem models, NASA Mars Fact Sheet parameters (6.36 mb pressure, ~0.38g gravity), and browser localStorage

Development & Deployment: Visual Studio Code, Node.js, Claude, Google Antigravity, and Vercel

How Is Our Project Creative?

Instead of building either a dry spreadsheet dashboard or a pure arcade shooter, Outpost Zero merges immersive first-person 3D exploration (inspired by Astroneer and survival games) with authentic NASA mission-control systems. Dynamic events physically transform the 3D world—dust storms darken the sky and coat solar panels, malfunctions trigger red warning beacons, and stepping outside the airlock shifts gravity to 0.38g—making every resource trade-off feel immediate and personal.

Key Factors We Considered

Scientific Integrity & Fallbacks: Ensuring API outages or rate limits never break the app by falling back to clearly labeled demonstration/historical datasets without ever faking live NASA telemetry.

Balanced, Meaningful Trade-Offs: Designing events with no "obvious perfect answer" so players must weigh short-term survival against long-term sustainability.

Modular Architecture & Security: Separating the 3D scene, simulation engine, and NASA API layer, and keeping credentials out of client-side code.

Usability & Accessibility: Adding a boot/loading screen, Continue/Start New Mission saves, a Pause Menu with sensitivity and quality controls, and clear doorway signage so beginners can navigate the outpost effortlessly.
